issues.description: The problem statement requires a method named checkOrderReady() to implement the order-serving logic, but the solution implements this functionality in a method named processOrders(). This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the solution will confuse students (and likely tests) about which method to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name/signature match the problem statement. Rename processOrders() to checkOrderReady() with the same visibility (public) and return type (void), and update all internal calls (e.g., orderMeal should call checkOrderReady()). Ensure the method implements the described FIFO serving behavior.

issues.description: The problem statement repeatedly refers to a method named checkOrderReady() (UML and text) as the routine that attempts to serve queued orders, but the solution implementation provides a method named processOrders() that implements this behavior. This naming divergence (checkOrderReady vs. processOrders) breaks the direct mapping between the requirement and the implementation and may confuse students about which method they must implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the order-serving method across artifacts. Rename the solution's processOrders() method to checkOrderReady() (and update orderMeal to call checkOrderReady()), or add a public checkOrderReady() wrapper that delegates to processOrders(), so the implementation matches the problem statement's API.
